case_name: Abhilasha Sharma And Others vs State Of H.P. And Others
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Complainant No.2's marriage was solemnized with accused No.1, but she took all valuables and did not return after 15 days. Complainants searched their house and found that valuable articles worth ₹15 lakhs were stolen.

legal_principles.principle: The Court should exercise the power under Section 228 of the Code very sparingly and with circumspection, and only in rare cases.
legal_principles.held: of Section 228 of the Code should be exercised very sparingly and with circumspection and that too in the rarest rt of rare cases.

legal_principles.principle: The Court should apply the test as to whether the uncontroverted allegations prima facie establish the offence or not.
legal_principles.held: The Court should apply the test as to whether the uncontroverted allegations as made from the record of the case and the documents submitted therewith prima facie establish the offence or not.

legal_principles.principle: The Court should not unduly interfere and meticulous examination of the evidence is not needed for considering whether the case would end in conviction or not at the stage of framing of charge or quashing of charge.
legal_principles.held: The High Court should not unduly interfere. No meticulous examination of the evidence is needed for considering whether the case would end in conviction or not at the stage of framing of charge or quashing of charge.

legal_principles.principle: The Court should balance the freedom of a person and the right of the complainant or prosecution to investigate and prosecute the offender.
legal_principles.held: The Court has a duty to balance the freedom of a person and the right of the complainant or prosecution to investigate and prosecute the offender.
